Reference - Authors: H E Gilleland; L B Gilleland; J Staczek; R N Harty; A García-Sastre; P Palese; F R Brennan; W D Hamilton; M Bendahmane; R N Beachy
Reference - Title: Chimeric animal and plant viruses expressing epitopes of outer membrane protein F as a combined vaccine against Pseudomonas aeruginosa lung infection.
Epitope - Comments: Peptide shown to provide protection to source species challenge in a mouse model of chronic pulmonary infection. No increase in protective efficacy was seen for the combined administration of another epitope (peptide 10) from source species. Swiss-Prot entry corresponds to the precursor protein while the positions given in the manuscript correspond to the mature form. This protein is antigenically conserved in all strains of source species.
1st immunogen - Dose Schedule: 3 immunizations 2 weeks apart. 1st: 50 micrograms of virions, 2nd: 10 micrograms, 3rd: 10 micrograms without adjuvant.
Immunization - Comments: 2 weeks after final immunization, 5 mice were sacrificed and sera was pooled for analysis of ELISA reactivity against epitope and source species.
Assay - Comments: Pooled serum from 5 mice immunized with recombinant tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) expressing epitope inserted in coat protein are shown to have high titers (>6400) of antibodies directed against the epitope and the source species, but not source species mutant lacking F protein. In mice infected with a mixture of this virus and a recombinant Influenza virus expressing peptide 10 from source protein, similar results are obtained. No reactivity is seen with the wild type carrier virus.

Absence of source species in lung tissue correlates with the lack of lesions.

Reference - Authors: W W Kum; A W Chow
Reference - Title: Inhibition of staphylococcal enterotoxin A-induced superantigenic and lethal activities by a monoclonal antibody to toxic shock syndrome toxin-1.
Immunization - Comments: Hybridomas were expanded in vitro and then were injected intraperitoneally into primed mice.  Monoclonal antibodies were purified from ascitic fluids.
Assay - Comments: The monoclonal antibody (MAb5) is a known anti-toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 antibody.  In further studies, Staphylococcal enterotoxin A was shown to be unable to inhibit toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 binding to MAb5 even at a concentration of 4500 nM. The monoclonal antibody (MAb5) is a known anti-toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 (TSST-1) antibody.  Epitope mapping of staphylococcus enterotoxin A (SEA), using overlapping decapeptides, revealed that MAb5 binds to a region on the SEA molecule corresponding to amino acid residues 154-161. This monoclonal antibody was also mapped to epitope sequences within both toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 and staphylococcal enterotoxin B.

Reference - Authors: J I Nishi; S Kanekura; S Takei; I Kitajima; T Nakajima; M R Wahid; K Masuda; M Yoshinaga; I Maruyama; K Miyata
Reference - Title: B cell epitope mapping of the bacterial superantigen staphylococcal enterotoxin B: the dominant epitope region recognized by intravenous IgG.
Immunization - Comments: Two commercially available pooled preparations of human IgG were used, Venilon-1 and Venoglobulin-IH.
Assay - Comments: Truncated and mutant forms of recombinant toxin were used to map the epitope recognized by a polyclonal preparation of i.v. human IgGs (either total or affinity purified against the C-terminal residues 133-239 of S.aureus enterotoxin B (SEB)) from healthy individuals. Deletion or mutation of this epitopic sequence highly disminishes recognition. These facts suggested that these residues are the dominant epitope recognized by i.v. IgGs. An epitope-specific polyclonal preparation of i.v. human IgGs (affinity purified against the C-terminal residues 133-239 of S.aureus enterotoxin B (SEB)) from healthy individuals is shown to have a disminished recogntion of other related toxins with substitutions at the epitopic sequence. The assay was performed with the different antigens bound to the ELISA plate or as a competitive ELISA where the different antigens compete the binding to SEB. These facts suggested that these residues are the dominant epitope recognized by i.v. IgGs.

Immunization - Comments: Human cell lines producing mAbs against P. aeruginosa exotoxin A were established by EBV transformation followed by cell fusion. Human peripheral blood lymphocytes collected from healthy volunteers with high anti-exotoxin A titers were infected for 2 weeks with EBV (M.O.I. = 2). Reference - Title: Titrating T-cell epitopes within self-assembled vaccines optimizes CD4+ helper T cell and antibody outputs.
1st immunogen - Dose Schedule: 1 dose of 200nmol, followed by 2 doses of 100nmol at 4 and 8 weeks
Immunization - Comments: Mice were immunized with the epitope linked by a SGSG linker sequence to the Q11 short assembly domain, QQKFQFQFEQQ, which forms beta-sheet nanofibers in water to create a self-adjuvanting vaccine (E214Q11). In some experiments, the E214Q11 was co-assembled with the PADREQ11 vaccine, containing the PADRE T-cell epitope (aKXVAAWTLKAa, where “X” is cyclohexylalanine and “a” is D-alanine).
Assay - Comments: Anti-epitope antibodies were only raised after immunization with the coassembled E214Q11/PADREQ11 vaccine, containing the PADRE T-cell epitope. Subsequent experiments revealed the Abs only recognized the epitope, not the PADRE epitope or Q11 sequence. Induction of a response required co-assembled vaccine fibers, suggesting the PADRE T cell epitope acts like a peptide-protein congjugate. Induction of the response did not require recruitment of inflammatory dendritic cells, neutrophils, or eosinophils. The peak response was observed at a concentration of 0.05 - 0.1 mM of the PADREQ11 vaccine. The Ab isotypes consisted primarily of a mixture of IgG1 and IgG2b. The epitope competed against itself in a competition ELISA, yielding IC50 values of approximately 0.6 μM and 2 μM IC50 at low and high densities of E214 coated on the ELISA plate. The epitope was also bound in direct ELISA.

Cells were screened via ELISA using S. aureus surface antigens to identify wells containing B cells secreting antigen-specific antibodies.
